Complete list of the academic sources, international guidelines, and national regulations (MSPyBS Paraguay) that support the content of the clinical reference guides in the CaVeSal® Medical Record. Each guide cites its source in short form at the bottom; here is the full detail, organized by topic area.

Index

  • 1. National official regulations (MSPyBS Paraguay)
  • 2. Reproductive physiology, gynecologic endocrinology, and the ovarian cycle
  • 3. Polycystic ovary syndrome and the infertile couple workup
  • 4. Benign uterine pathology, endometriosis, and endometrial ultrasound (IETA)
  • 5. Pelvic floor, menopause, hormone therapy, and bone health
  • 6. Perinatal medicine, obstetrics, and fetal surveillance
  • 7. Puberty and pubertal development
  • 8. Contraception, GLP-1/metformin therapies, and Vitamin D in reproductive health

🇵🇾 1. National official regulations (MSPyBS Paraguay)

Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS/SPGO). (2018). Manual Nacional de Normas de Atención de las Principales Patologías Obstétricas (1st ed.). Asunción, Paraguay.

Contribution: stepwise tocolytic management protocols, magnesium sulfate neuroprotection, fetal lung maturation, treatment of intrahepatic cholestasis, and management of prolonged pregnancy and fetal demise.

Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS). (2021). Guía de Manejo de la Hemorragia Posparto: Código Rojo Obstétrico (Resolution S.G. No. 2004/2021). Asunción, Paraguay.

Contribution: standardized roles, aggressive resuscitation, hypovolemic shock, and surgical/medical response times.

Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS). (2022). Manual de Cuidados Perinatales (Resolution S.G. No. 1078/2022). Asunción, Paraguay.

Contribution: tiered ("traffic-light") preconception counseling, prenatal care, partograph, and postpartum management; also supports the mention of the tiered scheme in the Preconception screening and folic acid guide and the Preconception risk traffic light (MSPBS 2022) guide, with cut-offs and folic acid doses verified on p. 23 of the Manual.

Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS). (2023). Orientaciones Técnicas para la Atención Integral a la Mujer en Climaterio (Resolution S.G. No. 267/2023). Asunción, Paraguay.

Contribution: MRS scale, ORAI, postmenopausal endometrial thickness, and menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) regimens.

Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS). (2025). Manual Nacional de Normas de Atención de Patologías Ginecológicas (Resolution S.G. No. 050/2025). Asunción, Paraguay.

Contribution: standardized algorithms for amenorrhea, precocious and delayed puberty, fibroids under the STEP-W classification, endometriosis (Law No. 7341/2024), pelvic floor pathology, and low-complexity ovulation induction.

Programa Ampliado de Inmunizaciones (PAI) Paraguay, Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social. HPV vaccine — official material, by-group schedule infographic. · World Health Organization, Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE). (2022, December). Human papillomavirus vaccines: WHO position paper. Weekly Epidemiological Record.

Contribution: Paraguay's HPV vaccination schedule by age group/risk group (ages 9-14, ages 15-24, risk groups ages 15-45) and its corroboration against the international SAGE position on 1-dose schedules in the general population and 2-3 dose schedules in immunocompromised individuals — basis for the HPV Vaccination guide.

🔬 2. Reproductive physiology, gynecologic endocrinology, and the ovarian cycle

Speroff, L., & Fritz, M. A. (2019). Clinical Gynecologic Endocrinology and Infertility (9th ed.). Lippincott Williams & Wilkins.

Contribution: follicular- and luteal-phase physiology, gonadotropin (LH/FSH) surges, the endometrial implantation window, basal body temperature curves, and diagnostic criteria for functional amenorrhea.

Mihm, M., Gangooly, S., & Muttukrishna, S. (2011). The normal menstrual cycle in women. Animal Reproduction Science, 124(3-4), 229–236.

Contribution: ultrasound and endocrine characterization of dominant follicle selection and luteolysis.

Melmed, S., Casanueva, F. F., Hoffman, A. R., et al. (2011). Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyperprolactinemia: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism, 96(2), 273–288.

Contribution: serum prolactin cutoffs, ruling out macroprolactin and the hook effect, cabergoline/bromocriptine dosing, and neuroimaging indications.

Vilar, L., Abucham, J., Albuquerque, J. L., et al. (2019). Results of an explicit guideline for the management of prolactinomas? A series of 285 patients. Pituitary, 22(5), 491–500.

Contribution: titration criteria, long-term efficacy, and transsphenoidal surgical management in resistance or tumor apoplexy.

🌸 3. Polycystic ovary syndrome and the infertile couple workup

Teede, H. J., Tay, C. T., Laven, J. J., et al. (2023). Recommendations from the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome. Fertility and Sterility, 120(4), 767–793.

Contribution: international diagnostic criteria, phenotypes A–D, transvaginal ultrasound follicle-count thresholds, AMH use, and comprehensive management.

The Rotterdam ESHRE/ASRM-Sponsored PCOS Consensus Workshop Group. (2004). Revised 2003 consensus on diagnostic criteria and long-term health risks related to polycystic ovary syndrome. Fertility and Sterility, 81(1), 19–25.

Contribution: definition of the three classic criteria (anovulation, clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic morphology).

Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM). (2021). Diagnostic evaluation of the infertile female: a committee opinion. Fertility and Sterility, 116(5), 1255–1265.

Contribution: pillars of ovarian reserve testing (FSH, estradiol, AMH, AFC), hysterosalpingography, and ovulation confirmation.

World Health Organization (WHO). (2021). WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen (6th ed.). Geneva: World Health Organization.

Contribution: minimum reference values for standard semen analysis (volume, concentration, progressive motility, vitality, and strict Kruger morphology).

Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM). (2013). Use of clomiphene citrate in infertile women: a committee opinion. Fertility and Sterility, 100, 341–348.

Contribution: clomiphene citrate ovulation-induction protocols, monitoring and follicle size for the hCG trigger (higher pregnancy rates with a leading follicle of 23-28mm).

Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM). (2020). Use of exogenous gonadotropins for ovulation induction in anovulatory women: a committee opinion. Fertility and Sterility, 113, 66–70.

Contribution: low-dose gonadotropin regimens, trigger at follicular maturity and cycle cancellation with more than two follicles >16mm.

Palatnik, A., Strawn, E., Szabo, A., & Robb, P. (2012). What is the optimal follicular size before triggering ovulation in intrauterine insemination cycles with clomiphene citrate or letrozole? An analysis of 988 cycles. Fertility and Sterility, 97, 1089–1094.

Contribution: higher pregnancy rates with a leading follicle of 23-28mm in clomiphene or letrozole cycles; 28mm tolerance limit.

Shalom-Paz, E., Marzal, A., Wiser, A., Hyman, J., & Tulandi, T. (2014). Does optimal follicular size in IUI cycles vary between clomiphene citrate and gonadotrophins treatments? Gynecological Endocrinology, 30(2), 107–110.

Contribution: clomiphene trigger from 20mm (leading follicle of 20.4 ± 1.2mm in conception cycles) and smaller size with gonadotropins.

Ling, L., et al. (2024). Effect of follicle size on pregnancy outcomes in patients undergoing first letrozole-intrauterine insemination. European Journal of Medical Research, 29, 184.

Contribution: optimal size of 19.1-21mm for the trigger in the first letrozole IUI cycle.

Van Oirschot, M., et al. (2025). Optimal follicle size for human chorionic gonadotropin trigger in mono-follicular growth during letrozole-induced intrauterine insemination cycles: findings from a large retrospective study. Fertility and Sterility.

Contribution: 19-23mm range for the hCG trigger in letrozole IUI cycles.

ESHRE Ovarian Stimulation Guideline Group. (2025). Ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI: guideline update 2025. European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology.

Contribution: the association between follicle size and outcome has not been sufficiently studied; the trigger size is individualized.

ESHRE Guideline Group on Female Infertility. (2023). Female infertility: a guideline. Human Reproduction Open, 2023(3), hoad034.

Contribution: serial ultrasound monitoring protocol for ovulation induction, baseline and serial folliculometry criteria, and definition of induction resistance/treatment failure.

Facchinetti, F., et al. (2020). Reduction of oocyte quality and clinical outcomes using myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol: an update. Expert Opinion on Drug Metabolism & Toxicology. · Unfer, V., et al. (2017). Myo-inositol effects in women with PCOS: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Endocrine Connections. · Cochrane. (2023 update). Inositol for subfertility associated with PCOS (Review). · ESHRE/ASRM/Monash PCOS Guideline (2023).

Contribution: mechanism, dosing (myo-inositol 2-4g/day, physiological 40:1 ratio with D-chiro-inositol), and low-to-moderate certainty evidence on improved ovulation/clinical pregnancy rates in PMOS — basis for the Myo-inositol guide (see also Chapter 8, inadvertent exposure during fertility recovery).

Poyatos-León, R., Martínez-Vizcaíno, V., Sequí-Domínguez, I., Sanabria-Martínez, G., Díez Fernández, A., & Martínez-Hortelano, J. A. (2026). The effect of myo-inositol supplementation on gestational diabetes mellitus prevention: a systematic review and meta-analysis. American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, 235(5), 1024–1036. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2026.05.020

Contribution: most recent, specific meta-analysis on myo-inositol and gestational diabetes prevention — 12 RCTs, 4,765 women without preexisting diabetes, 44% relative risk reduction for GDM, no significant differences in hypertensive disorders/cesarean/macrosomia/preterm birth/neonatal hypoglycemia; cited in the Myo-inositol guide.

World Health Organization. (2024). Guideline on haemoglobin cutoffs to define anaemia in individuals and populations. Geneva: WHO. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240088542

Contribution: anemia in non-pregnant women below 12 g/dL (mild 11–11.9; severe <8); basis for yellow between 11 and 12 in the Preconception risk traffic light.

American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists & Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. (2022, reaffirmed 2025). Pregnancy at age 35 years or older. Obstetric Care Consensus No. 11. Obstetrics & Gynecology. https://www.acog.org/clinical/guidance/obstetric-care-consensus/2022/08/pregnancy-at-age-35-years-or-older

Contribution: age 35 or older as a risk factor; resolves age 35 in the MSPBS traffic light as yellow.

Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2026). MTHFR Gene Variant and Folic Acid Facts. https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/data-research/mthfr/index.html

Contribution: with an MTHFR variant, folic acid at the same dose; it is the only form of folate shown to prevent neural tube defects.

Bashford, M. T., Hickey, S. E., Curry, C. J., Toriello, H. V., & ACMG Professional Practice and Guidelines Committee. (2020). Addendum: ACMG Practice Guideline: lack of evidence for MTHFR polymorphism testing. Genetics in Medicine, 22(12), 2125. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41436-020-0843-0

Contribution: do not order MTHFR testing (2013 document reaffirmed in 2020).

American College of Radiology. (2023). O-RADS US v2022 Assessment Categories. Strachowski, M. J., et al. Radiology, 308(3), e230685. https://cs.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/RADS/O-RADS/US-v2022/O-RADS--US-v2022-Assessment-Categories.pdf

Contribution: O-RADS v2022 categories and management (Ovarian tumor guide).

Amor, F., Vaccaro, H., Alcázar, J. L., et al. (2009). Gynecologic imaging reporting and data system. Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine, 28(3), 285–291. https://doi.org/10.7863/jum.2009.28.3.285

Contribution: GI-RADS categories (GI-RADS guide).

Ray-Coquard, I., Morice, P., Lorusso, D., et al. (2018). Non-epithelial ovarian cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines. Annals of Oncology, 29(Suppl 4), iv1–iv18. https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-clinical-practice-guideline-non-epithelial-ovarian-cancer

Contribution: AFP, hCG, LDH and inhibin B in germ cell and sex cord-stromal tumors (Ovarian tumors by origin and markers guide).

Ledermann, J. A., Matias-Guiu, X., Amant, F., et al. (2024). ESGO–ESMO–ESP consensus conference recommendations on ovarian cancer. Annals of Oncology, 35(3), 248–266. https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esgo-esmo-esp-consensus-recommendations-ovarian-cancer

Contribution: BRCA/HRD, surgery and maintenance; no marker alone distinguishes benign from malignant (ovarian guides).

Prat, J. (2014). Staging classification for cancer of the ovary, fallopian tube, and peritoneum. International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics, 124(1), 1–5. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijgo.2013.10.001

Contribution: FIGO 2014 ovarian stages.

Berek, J. S., Matias-Guiu, X., Creutzberg, C., et al. (2023). FIGO staging of endometrial cancer: 2023. International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics, 162(2), 383–394. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10482588/

Contribution: FIGO 2023 endometrial stages with molecular group.

Concin, N., et al. (2025). ESGO–ESTRO–ESP guidelines for the management of patients with endometrial carcinoma: update 2025. Lancet Oncology. https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanonc/article/PIIS1470-2045(25)00167-6/fulltext

Contribution: management by molecular risk group in endometrial cancer.

Cibula, D., Raspollini, M. R., Planchamp, F., et al. (2023). ESGO/ESTRO/ESP guidelines for the management of patients with cervical cancer – Update 2023. International Journal of Gynecological Cancer, 33, 649–666. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10247855/

Contribution: pelvic MRI, PET-CT and stage-based management in cervical cancer.

Harmsen, M. J., Van den Bosch, T., de Leeuw, R. A., et al. (2022). Consensus on revised definitions of MUSA features of adenomyosis. Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology, 60(1), 118–131. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9328356/

Contribution: direct and indirect features; the 12 mm junctional zone cut-off is withdrawn (Adenomyosis guide).

International Society for Gynecologic Endoscopy. (2023). Hysteroscopic myomectomy: the guidelines (STEP-W). https://isge.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/ISGE_Hysteroscopic_myomectomy_The_guidelines.pdf

Contribution: STEP-W score (Fibroids guide).

American College of Radiology. (2025). ACR BI-RADS® v2025 Manual. https://www.appliedradiology.com/news/acr-releases-bi-rads-v2025-manual-detailing-reporting-and-lexicon-updates-across-modalities

Contribution: split category 0 and management by category (BI-RADS guides).

ASCCP. (2024–2025). Enduring guidelines process: dual stain, self-collection and extended genotyping. https://www.asccp.org/guidelines/management-guidelines-enduring-guidelines-process/enduring-guidelines-process/

Contribution: p16/Ki-67 dual stain and HPV self-collection (ASCCP guide).

🩺 4. Benign uterine pathology, endometriosis, and endometrial ultrasound (IETA)

Leone, F. P., Timmerman, D., Bourne, T., et al. (2010). Terms, definitions and measurements to describe the sonographic features of the endometrium and intrauterine lesions: a consensus opinion from the International Endometrial Tumor Analysis (IETA) group. Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology, 35(1), 103–112.

Contribution: standardized endometrial thickness measurement, echogenicity classification, definition of the endometrial-myometrial junction, and vascular patterns (Color Score 1–4).

Epstein, E., Fischerova, D., Valentin, L., et al. (2018). Ultrasound characteristics of endometrial cancer as defined by International Endometrial Tumor Analysis (IETA) consensus: prospective cohort study. Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology, 51(6), 818–828.

Contribution: clinical validation of chaotic/branching Doppler flow and irregular borders for detecting malignant pathology.

American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG). (2018). Committee Opinion No. 734: The Role of Transvaginal Ultrasonography in Evaluating the Endometrium of Postmenopausal Patients with Abnormal Uterine Bleeding. Obstetrics & Gynecology, 131(5), e124–e129.

Contribution: ≤4mm ultrasound threshold in postmenopausal bleeding (NPV >99%) and indications for outpatient endometrial biopsy (Pipelle).

Revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM). (1997). Revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine classification of endometriosis: 1996. Fertility and Sterility, 67(5), 817–821.

Contribution: endometriosis stages I–IV based on scoring of peritoneal implants, endometriomas, and pelvic adhesions.

Keckstein, J., Saridogan, E., Ulrich, U. A., et al. (2021). The #Enzian classification: A comprehensive directory of deep endometriosis and its associated diseases. Human Reproduction Open, 2021(4), hoab038.

Contribution: standardized mapping of deep retroperitoneal endometriosis by anatomic compartments (A, B, C, and affected organs).

Munro, M. G., Critchley, H. O., Fraser, I. S., & FIGO Menstrual Disorders Committee. (2018). The two FIGO systems for normal and abnormal uterine bleeding symptoms and classification of causes of abnormal uterine bleeding in the reproductive years, including PALM-COEIN. International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics, 143(3), 393–408.

Contribution: morphologic subclassification of uterine fibroids, FIGO types 0–8.

🌷 5. Pelvic floor, menopause, hormone therapy, and bone health

Bump, R. C., Mattiasson, A., Bø, K., et al. (1996). The standardization of terminology of female pelvic organ prolapse and pelvic floor dysfunction. American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, 175(1), 10–17.

Contribution: pelvic organ prolapse quantification system (POP-Q) and standardized clinical staging (grades 0–IV).

Heinemann, K., Ruebig, A., Potthoff, P., et al. (2004). The Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) scale: A methodological review. Health and Quality of Life Outcomes, 2, 45.

Contribution: validation of the somatic, psychological, and urogenital domains, and severity cutoffs for menopausal syndrome.

Heinemann, L. A. J., Do, M. T., Strelow, F., Gerbsch, S., Schnitker, J., & Schneider, H. P. G. (2004). The Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) as outcome measure for hormone treatment? A validation study. Health and Quality of Life Outcomes, 2, 67. doi:10.1186/1477-7525-2-67

Contribution: severity cutoffs for the total and for each domain (no/little symptoms, mild, moderate, severe) and validation of the scale as an outcome measure for hormone treatment.

The 2022 Hormone Therapy Position Statement of The North American Menopause Society (NAMS). (2022). Menopause, 29(7), 767–794.

Contribution: window-of-opportunity criteria (age <60 or <10 years postmenopause), regimens with and without progestogen opposition, and absolute contraindications.

Stute, P., et al. (2026). 'Healthy menopause': The European Menopause and Andropause Society (EMAS) 2026 framework for precision, digital, and interdisciplinary midlife health. Maturitas, 212, 109060.

Contribution: multidisciplinary approach to healthy aging, metabolic stratification, and pharmacologic alternatives.

Anagnostis, P., Bosdou, J. K., Georgiou, T., & Goulis, D. G. (2025). Can menopausal hormone therapy be considered in postmenopausal women who are older than 60 years? Gynecological Endocrinology, 41(1), 2468957.

Contribution: safety guidance, ultra-low-dose transdermal therapy for refractory severe vasomotor symptoms, and non-hormonal preference after age 60.

Pratt, M. C., et al. (2023). Fezolinetant for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause. Expert Review of Clinical Pharmacology, 16(5), 389–398.

Contribution: NK3 receptor blockade at the hypothalamic level (KNDy neurons) as first-line non-hormonal therapy for hot flashes.

American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG). (2026). Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13 — Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms. Obstetrics & Gynecology, 148(5), e345–e364. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42878500/

Contribution: dosing tables for systemic HRT and the tissue-selective estrogen complex (CEE+bazedoxifene), the non-hormonal options table (SSRI/SNRI, fezolinetant, elinzanetant, gabapentin) with the exact liver-monitoring cadence per drug, graded recommendations for non-pharmacologic interventions (CBT, mindfulness, exercise, clinical hypnosis, acupuncture), and an explicit non-recommendation statement on phytoestrogens/herbal supplements — basis for the MRS Scale and HRT, Fezolinetant and elinzanetant, and Climacteric — non-pharmacologic management guides.

Knapen, M. H. J., Drummen, N. E., Smit, E., Vermeer, C., & Theuwissen, E. (2013). Three-year low-dose menaquinone-7 supplementation helps decrease bone loss in healthy postmenopausal women. Osteoporosis International, 24(9), 2499–2507.

Contribution: randomized trial (n=244, 3 years) of vitamin K2 (MK-7) 180mcg/day in healthy postmenopausal women — decreased bone mineral density loss at the lumbar spine and femoral neck — basis for the Vitamin K2 (MK-7) guide.

Vossen, L. M., de Leeuw, P. W., Schurgers, L. J., et al. (2026). Two Years of Menaquinone-7 Supplementation and Coronary Artery Calcification: A Randomized Clinical Trial (VitaK-CAC). JAMA Cardiology (online, June 10, 2026).

Contribution: randomized trial (n=167, 2 years) of vitamin K2 (MK-7) 360mcg/day in patients with symptomatic coronary artery disease — modest slowing of coronary calcification progression, an effect the authors themselves describe as of still-uncertain clinical significance — basis for the Vitamin K2 (MK-7) guide.

McClung, M. R., & Clark, A. L. (2026). Preventing menopause-related bone loss (Menopause Step-by-Step). Menopause, 33(11), 1209–1211. https://doi.org/10.1097/GME.0000000000002931

Contribution: prevention of menopause-related bone loss: risk predictors, DXA in perimenopausal women with risk factors, limits of supplements and exercise, estrogen doses, management when MHT is stopped and alternatives — basis of the Prevention block of the Osteoporosis guide.

Bolland, M. J., Nisa, Z., Mellar, A., et al. (2025). Fracture prevention with infrequent zoledronate in women 50 to 60 years of age. New England Journal of Medicine, 392, 239–248. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2407031

Contribution: infrequent zoledronic acid in women aged 50 to 60 years to prevent fractures — support for a short bisphosphonate course when estrogen is stopped.

The North American Menopause Society. (2021). Management of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women: the 2021 position statement. Menopause, 28, 973–997. https://doi.org/10.1097/GME.0000000000001831

Contribution: The Menopause Society position on postmenopausal osteoporosis management, including estrogen for prevention.

The North American Menopause Society. (2022). The 2022 hormone therapy position statement. Menopause, 29, 767–794. https://doi.org/10.1097/GME.0000000000002028

Contribution: The Menopause Society position on hormone therapy — use to prevent bone loss in high-risk women even without vasomotor symptoms.

US Preventive Services Task Force, Mangione, C. M., Barry, M. J., Nicholson, W. K., et al. (2022). Hormone therapy for the primary prevention of chronic conditions in postmenopausal persons: recommendation statement. JAMA, 328, 1740–1746. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.18625

Contribution: recommendation against hormone therapy for the primary prevention of chronic conditions — opposing position cited in the Osteoporosis guide.

Benedetto, C., Gulati, M., Khadilkar, S. S., Maas, A. H. E. M., Frezet, F., Moraes de Oliveira, G. M., Genazzani, A. R., Divakar, H., & Poppas, A., on behalf of the World Heart Federation (WHF) and the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO). (2026). Menopause hormone therapy in women with cardiovascular risk factors or established ischemic heart disease: A joint FIGO and WHF position paper. International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1002/ijgo.71356

Contribution: joint FIGO/WHF position — cardiovascular risk-stratification algorithm before prescribing MHT (coronary artery calcium score by CT for intermediate risk), specific management in established ischemic heart disease (INOCA, MINOCA, obstructive coronary disease, spontaneous coronary artery dissection) and differentiated VTE/stroke risk by progestogen type — underpins the new MHT and cardiovascular risk (FIGO/WHF) guide.

🤰 6. Perinatal medicine, obstetrics, and fetal surveillance

International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology (ISUOG). Practice Guidelines (updated): performance of the routine mid-trimester fetal ultrasound scan. (2022). Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology, 59(6), 840–856. — and its predecessors, ISUOG Practice Guidelines: sonographic examination of the fetal central nervous system (2020) and fetal heart screening examination (2023).

Contribution: technical framework and system-by-system checklist for the Fetal structural morphology — 7 systems guide (CNS, face, spine, heart, abdomen, limbs).

Paladini, D., & Volpe, P. (2018). Ultrasound of Congenital Fetal Anomalies: Differential Diagnosis and Prognostic Indicators (3rd ed.). CRC Press.

Contribution: detailed diagnostic criteria and management for each structural finding (ventriculomegaly, lemon/strawberry sign, cardiac defects, CDH, wall defects).

Jeanty, P., Dramaix-Wilmet, M., Elkhazen, N., Hubinont, C., & van Regemorter, N. (1984). Measurements of fetal orbits and binocular distance in normal pregnancy. Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine, 3(6), 241–244. · Mayden, K. L., Tortora, M., Berkowitz, R. L., Bracken, M., & Hobbins, J. C. (1982). Orbital diameters: a new parameter for prenatal diagnosis and dating. American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, 144(3), 289–297.

Contribution: orbital diameter (IOD/OOD) reference tables and the "rule of thirds" for hyper/hypotelorism — Face field of the Fetal structural morphology guide.

Corteville, J. E., Gray, D. L., & Crane, J. P. (1991). Congenital hydronephrosis: correlation of fetal ultrasonographic findings with infant outcome. American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, 165(2), 384–388. · Corteville, J. E., Dicke, J. M., & Crane, J. P. (1992). Fetal pyelectasis and Down syndrome: is genetic amniocentesis warranted? Obstetrics & Gynecology, 79(5), 770–772.

Contribution: renal pelvis dilation cutoffs by AP diameter (GA-dependent at 33 weeks) — Abdomen field of the Fetal structural morphology guide.

CDHSG — Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Study Group / Jani, J., Nicolaides, K. H., Keller, R. L., et al. (2007). Observed to expected lung area to head circumference ratio in the prediction of survival in fetuses with isolated diaphragmatic hernia. Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology, 30(1), 67–71.

Contribution: O/E LHR as a severity predictor in congenital diaphragmatic hernia — Chest and heart field of the Fetal structural morphology guide.

Jauniaux, E., Bhide, A., Kennedy, A., et al. — FIGO Placenta Accreta Spectrum Expert Consensus Panel. (2018). FIGO consensus guidelines on placenta accreta spectrum disorders: Prenatal diagnosis and screening. International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics, 140(3), 274–280. · Jauniaux, E., Collins, S., & Burton, G. J. (2016). Placenta accreta spectrum: pathophysiology and evidence-based anatomy for prenatal ultrasound imaging. American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, 215(3), 712–721.

Contribution: risk factors, 2D ultrasound signs (clear zone, lacunae, bladder-uterine interface), and the surgical/histopathological FIGO classification (grades 1-3b) — basis for the Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) guide.

American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) & Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM). (2018, reaffirmed 2021). Obstetric Care Consensus No. 7: Placenta Accreta Spectrum. Obstetrics & Gynecology, 132(6), e259–e275.

Contribution: management of suspected PAS (never manual placental removal, placenta left in situ + en bloc hysterectomy, Level III-IV center, planned cesarean at 34+0-35+6 weeks) — the "golden rule" of the PAS guide.
